critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: When the next target cannot be localized from current images, use its retained center rather than guessing from the blank tabletop. Here, with the blue cube held at clearance and zero visits, command the right center at z=0.10 m, preserving orientation and the closed grasp.

More precise localization of the left target's circular center was needed. At this cycle the center corresponds to approximately world (x=-0.1199, y=0.2170), not (-0.1308, 0.2193). Use the center of the circular target marking, excluding the adjacent green cube, for calibrated tabletop projection; then move there at z=0.10 while preserving orientation and the closed grasp. The visit-count transition was already correct.

The close-empty-gripper rule should require correcting lateral alignment to the button's nominal approach center before applying its 5 mm upward fallback. Here the current TCP was about 2 cm off in x; use the visible button geometry to command [-0.2141, -0.1862, 0.15] and close, rather than treating the current x,y as aligned and only raising z.

Before descending to press, re-localize the button center from the current calibrated wrist image rather than preserving the current TCP x,y merely because the hand is approximately above it. Here the button center is approximately x=-0.2141, y=-0.1862, about 2 cm in +x from the current TCP. Command that corrected x,y at z=0.0075 with the gripper remaining closed.

At the pickup hover, recompute the cube's horizontal center rather than preserving the hover TCP x,y. Back-project the green top-face center in the current wrist image onto the cube's top surface (approximately z=0.04 m), then use that x,y for the grasp at TCP z=0.02 m. Here this gives approximately x=-0.0337, y=-0.0925; the hover x=-0.0484 is not sufficiently aligned. The cube top's projection height must not be confused with the TCP grasp height.

The button-localization rule needed a precise reference surface and height for calibrated projection, rather than just saying to account for its raised surface. Here the button approach should be centered at world x=-0.1515, y=0.1315, with z=0.15 and the hand open; my estimated center (-0.14, 0.137) was inaccurate. This is a visible-geometry localization issue, not missing visit history.

Before descending to press, re-localize the button center from the current calibrated wrist image rather than using the current TCP x,y as its center. Being approximately above the button does not establish lateral alignment. Here the press should correct to x=-0.2331, y=-0.0125 while descending to z=0.0075 with the gripper closed; retaining TCP x=-0.2443, y=-0.0065 misses that correction.

annotator_prompt.name: right_target_center
annotator_prompt.description: After the instructed cube was lifted, the right target marking could be obscured although the visit count correctly required the first right visit. The policy guessed a different tabletop location. The existing memory therefore failed SUFFICIENCY. Add a field holding the fixed right target center as [x, y] in world metres. Initialize it from the first cycle in which the circular marking is clearly localizable using calibrated images and the tabletop plane; in these recordings this is the initial cycle. Retain that value thereafter, including while the marking is occluded. Use null before any such observation. Annotate from the visible marking, not from a later commanded waypoint or the actual arrival TCP. Example: [-0.0761, -0.1789].

annotator_prompt.name: button_center
annotator_prompt.description: After the final cube release and retreat, the button could be obscured by the arm. The completed visit count remained correct, but the policy guessed a remote approach location because it had not retained the previously visible button location. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. Add a field holding the fixed button center as [x, y] in world metres. Initialize it at the first cycle with a clearly localizable button cap or base, which is the initial cycle in these recordings, and retain it thereafter. Use null before such an observation. Obtain the center from calibrated visible geometry at its surface height, not from the subsequent recorded action or the tracking-error-displaced TCP. Example: [-0.1759, 0.1970].

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: right_target_center
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: A lifted cube and hand can hide the right marking just when target_visits requires moving there; counting visits alone then fails SUFFICIENCY. When this field is empty and the right circular target is clearly visible in the current cycle, locate the center of its concentric marking and back-project it onto the tabletop using the supplied calibration. Write its world [x, y], for example [-0.0761, -0.1789]. Right is the smaller-world-y target. Exclude nearby cubes when fitting the marking. Until localization is possible write null; once initialized retain the value, especially through occlusion. Do not replace it with the TCP position at an arrival.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: button_center
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: The button may disappear behind the arm after the cube is released, leaving the completed visit count insufficient to select the button approach. To restore SUFFICIENCY, initialize this field whenever it is empty and the current images clearly show the button's circular cap or square base. Store its calibrated world center [x, y], for example [-0.1759, 0.1970], and retain it thereafter. For the cap center use its raised top plane, approximately z=0.03 m; do not project it onto the tabletop or the commanded press height. A base-based estimate must use the base's own surface plane. Write null until a reliable observation exists. Never substitute the current hand position for the button center.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
The alternating-visit count and its observed-arrival transitions were correct; leave those rules unchanged. Failures occurred when the required destination was hidden, and when an approximately aligned hand or a feature projected at the wrong height was mistaken for the destination center. These are SUFFICIENCY failures of the spatial action rules, not reasons to add a task-phase counter.

For a right-target visit, use right_target_center when the current marking is obscured rather than guessing a location on blank tabletop. Continue to command z=0.10 m with the grasp maintained. For either target that is visible, localize the center of the concentric circular marking, excluding adjacent cubes; project the marking onto the tabletop, not onto the carried cube's plane. A neighboring colored cube must not shift the estimated target center.

At the pickup hover, replace any interpretation that descent preserves the reported hover TCP x,y with explicit visual recentering: back-project the center of the cube's top face onto approximately z=0.04 m, then command that horizontal center at TCP z=0.02 m and close. The top-face projection height and grasp TCP height are different. Ordinary hover tracking error is not evidence that the hand is centered.

For the button approach after release and clearance, use button_center if the button is hidden. If visible, localize the circular cap center with its approximately z=0.03 m raised top plane and the current camera calibration. Do not project the cap onto the tabletop, the approach plane, or the commanded press depth. Command the resulting button x,y at z=0.15 m, downward orientation and yaw zero, with the hand open.

For closing the empty gripper above the button, explicitly command the button's nominal x,y and z=0.15 m while closing, correcting lateral tracking error in that same action. Apply the 5 mm upward fallback only if this full nominal positional waypoint is within 2 mm of the reported TCP; do not use the fallback instead of correcting x,y. Before pressing, likewise use the visible calibrated button center, or its retained center if obscured, at commanded z=0.0075 m with the gripper closed. Being approximately above the button does not authorize copying current TCP x,y. Keep the existing contact-triggered retraction rule, retracting to the button center at z=0.15 m rather than repeatedly descending.
proposal.refused: The request to retain both target centers is only partly supported. The right marking became unavailable when its location was needed, so its center is added. The reported left-target miss occurred with the marking still visible beside another cube; that requires precise localization, not additional historical memory. Adding a left-target-center field for these failures would violate NECESSITY. No episode-specific waypoint constants are added to the action rules: the locations vary across scenes and must come from calibrated observations.

fields.name: target_visits
fields.description: Initialize to 0 when memory is empty. Let N be the repetition count in the instruction. If the carried-in count is below 2N, the next uncounted target is right for an even count and left for an odd count. Increment once when this cycle shows the instructed cube held above that target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m, with the target activated red. Use the current endpoint and motion frames to confirm arrival; an activation on the other side is not a new visit. Otherwise retain the count, including during release and button operations. Never increment merely because a waypoint is being issued, and never increment on a zero-step unchanged cycle. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Number of completed, ordered target visits while holding the instructed cube. Start at 0. Count arrivals in the order right, left, right, left, up to twice the requested repetition count. A visit is completed when the carried cube arrives above the corresponding target at TCP height approximately 0.10 m and that target activates red. Record the increment at the cycle showing that arrival, not at the cycle commanding it. Do not count repeated frames of an activation, pickup, release, or button operations. Retain the final count thereafter. Thus all episodes have 0 at cycles 1–4; subsequent arrival cycles have 1, 2, 3, 4, and, for three repetitions, 5, 6. e.g. 2

texts.action:
Start with empty memory, an open hand, and target_visits initialized to zero. Read the cube color and repetition count N from the instruction. Update target_visits from observed arrivals before selecting the action; do not anticipate completion of the action you are about to issue. Right means smaller world y, appearing on the left of the front image; left means larger world y. Locate the two circular targets, the instructed cube, and the gray button on its square base using the calibrated images. Convert image locations to world coordinates using their appropriate surface heights, rather than treating image displacement as world displacement. Use the wrist view for fine localization. For either visible target, localize the center of its concentric circular marking, excluding neighboring cubes, and project onto the tabletop plane, not the carried cube's plane. If the right marking is obscured, use right_target_center from memory rather than guessing from blank tabletop. Localize the cube using its top-face plane, approximately z=0.04 m. For a visible button, project the circular cap center using its raised top plane, approximately z=0.03 m; a square-base estimate must use the base's own surface plane. Never project the cap onto the tabletop, approach plane, or press depth. If the button is obscured, use button_center from memory. Use newly observed centers when initializing these fields in the current cycle; a null field supplies no location. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.

When target_visits is zero and the instructed cube is not held, approach vertically above its center at z=0.15 m, gripper open, with roll approximately pi, pitch zero and yaw aligned to its square edges. If already above it at that height, visually recenter before descending: back-project the cube's top-face center onto approximately z=0.04 m, then command that horizontal center at TCP z=0.02 m and close. The projection plane and grasp TCP height are different. Do not copy the reported hover TCP x,y merely because it is approximately aligned; correct ordinary hover tracking error in the descent. A grasp is evidenced by the cube between the fingers and finger positions approximately 0.018–0.019 m, rather than an empty fully closed hand. When the newly grasped cube is still low, lift vertically to z=0.15 m, maintaining the grasp and cube-aligned orientation.

When holding the cube clear of the table and target_visits is less than 2N, command the center of the next required target at z=0.10 m: right if target_visits is even, left if odd. Keep the gripper closed and preserve the current orientation. Move directly between target centers at this height; do not lower onto the table, release, return to the pickup position, or insert a lift between visits. A confirmed red activation counts as arrival despite ordinary TCP tracking error; do not demand exact coincidence with the commanded coordinates. If the required target has not activated and arrival is uncertain, refine its center from visible geometry and complete that same visit rather than skipping it.

When target_visits equals 2N and the cube is still held at the final left target, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.07 m and open. When the cube has been released and the open hand remains low there, retreat vertically to approximately z=0.15 m while staying open. When the released cube is on the final target and the hand is clear, move above the button center at z=0.15 m, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper while commanding the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m, correcting lateral tracking error in that same action. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion: only if the full nominal positional waypoint is within 2 mm of the reported TCP, command the same button x,y at z=0.155 m instead. Do not use the upward fallback instead of correcting x,y. When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the calibrated visible button center, or button_center if obscured, to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation. Being approximately above the button does not authorize copying current TCP x,y. Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract to the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured, rather than the contact-displaced TCP x,y.

For an ambiguous or otherwise unmatched situation, use current images and gripper state to recover the applicable geometric condition: refine alignment, or raise vertically to safe clearance if low and obstructed. Preserve a held cube and the visit count. Do not invent completed visits or restart the alternating sequence. Never issue an identical-pose action, and do not wait without an observable task-related purpose.

annotator_prompt.description: Fixed center of the robot-right circular target, stored as [x, y] in world metres. Use null until the first cycle whose calibrated images clearly localize the concentric tabletop marking. At that cycle, record its center projected onto the tabletop plane, excluding neighboring cubes. Right is the smaller-world-y target. Retain this value thereafter, including through occlusion. Do not derive it from future frames, commanded waypoints, or arrival TCP positions. e.g. [-0.08, -0.18]

Fixed button center, stored as [x, y] in world metres. Use null until the first cycle whose calibrated images clearly localize the circular cap or square base. At that cycle, record the horizontal center using the observed feature's surface plane: approximately z=0.03 m for the cap, or the base's own surface height for the base. Retain this value thereafter, including through occlusion. Do not derive it from future frames, commanded waypoints, or TCP positions. e.g. [-0.18, 0.20]

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Initialize to null. While null, inspect the current cycle's calibrated images for the robot-right target, the smaller-world-y target. When its concentric circular marking is clearly localizable, exclude neighboring cubes and project the marking's center onto the tabletop plane; store world [x, y] in metres. Otherwise keep null. Once initialized, retain the value unchanged, including through occlusion; never replace it with a commanded waypoint or arrival TCP position. e.g. [-0.08, -0.18]

Initialize to null. While null, inspect the current cycle's calibrated images for a clearly localizable button cap or square base. Project the feature's center using its own surface plane, approximately z=0.03 m for the cap or the base's own surface height for the base, and store world [x, y] in metres. Otherwise keep null. Once initialized, retain the value unchanged, including through occlusion; never substitute a commanded waypoint or the hand position. e.g. [-0.18, 0.20]

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Target centers lie essentially on the tabletop; account for the cube's height when estimating its center and for the button's raised surface when localizing it. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: For either visible target, localize the center of its concentric circular marking, excluding neighboring cubes, and project onto the tabletop plane, not the carried cube's plane. If the right marking is obscured, use right_target_center from memory rather than guessing from blank tabletop. Localize the cube using its top-face plane, approximately z=0.04 m. For a visible button, project the circular cap center using its raised top plane, approximately z=0.03 m; a square-base estimate must use the base's own surface plane. Never project the cap onto the tabletop, approach plane, or press depth. If the button is obscured, use button_center from memory. Use newly observed centers when initializing these fields in the current cycle; a null field supplies no location. Do not reuse coordinates from another episode.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If already above it at that height, descend to its center at z=0.02 m and close.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: If already above it at that height, visually recenter before descending: back-project the cube's top-face center onto approximately z=0.04 m, then command that horizontal center at TCP z=0.02 m and close. The projection plane and grasp TCP height are different. Do not copy the reported hover TCP x,y merely because it is approximately aligned; correct ordinary hover tracking error in the descent.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper at the button's nominal approach position. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion; if that nominal position is too close to the reported TCP, add a 5 mm upward displacement.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: When already above the button with an open hand, close the empty gripper while commanding the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m, correcting lateral tracking error in that same action. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured. Ensure at least 2 mm of positional motion: only if the full nominal positional waypoint is within 2 mm of the reported TCP, command the same button x,y at z=0.155 m instead. Do not use the upward fallback instead of correcting x,y.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the button center to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: When above the button with the empty gripper closed, descend at the calibrated visible button center, or button_center if obscured, to commanded z=0.0075 m, retaining the closed gripper and downward orientation. Being approximately above the button does not authorize copying current TCP x,y.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract above the same button to z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Physical button contact may stop the actual TCP around z=0.024–0.025 m; when the cycle shows this low contact after the descent, retract to the localized button center x,y at z=0.15 m with the gripper closed, rather than repeatedly pressing downward. Use the calibrated visible center, or button_center if obscured, rather than the contact-displaced TCP x,y.

applied.refused: No left-target-center field or task-phase counter is added: the reported left-target error occurred with the marking visible and is addressed by feature-specific localization, while visit-count transitions were correct. Episode-specific destination coordinates are not committed; all destinations come from calibrated observations. No earlier edits are undone.
